entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Raimondo Guglielmo des Fargues was a 14th-century French priest and Cardinal, a nephew of Pope Clement V. He served as Archdeacon of Leicester from 1310 until his death in 1346, playing a significant role in the ecclesiastical hierarchy of medieval Europe. As a prominent figure in the Church, des Fargues was involved in various diplomatic efforts and played a key role in the governance of the English Church during the late Middle Ages.

As a representative of the Catholic Church, des Fargues contributed to the governance of the Church in England, shaping the religious landscape of the region. His influence extended beyond his own role, as he played a part in the politics of the Church in Western Europe.

Furthermore, des Fargues was a member of the College of Cardinals, participating in the papal conclave that elected Pope Clement VI in 1342. This appointment highlights his importance within the Catholic hierarchy during the 14th century.

In addition to his clerical roles, des Fargues was involved in various diplomatic efforts, including the negotiations between the English and French monarchs during the Hundred Years' War. His participation in these negotiations underscores his influence on the politics of Western Europe during this period.


The legacy of des Fargues can be seen in the continued influence of the Catholic Church in the governance of England during the late Middle Ages. His contributions to the Church's diplomatic efforts and governance of the English Church have left a lasting impact on the religious landscape of the region.


The role of des Fargues in the history of the Catholic Church highlights the importance of understanding the complex web of power and influence within the Church during the 14th century. His involvement in various diplomatic efforts and governance of the English Church underscores the significance of his contributions to the Church's development during this period.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Des Fargues played a key role in the governance of the English Church during the late Middle Ages, contributing to the continued influence of the Catholic Church in the region. His diplomatic efforts, including his participation in the negotiations between the English and French monarchs during the Hundred Years' War, had a lasting impact on the politics of Western Europe during this period.
